title: Supreme Court Says Border Wall Work Can Go On in West Texas
summary:
On Monday, the U.S. Supreme Court said work on border walls in west Texas can keep going while a court case about the plans is still being decided. The decision opens the way for hundreds of miles of walls and security work in the Big Bend area, including land inside Big Bend National Park.

The court's five-page decision was unsigned, which means no judge signed it as the writer. It said the judge in El Paso who had stopped the work did not have the power to do so. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson was the only judge who disagreed.

The judge's stop had paused work on 30-foot-tall steel walls, patrol roads, and camera systems that watch the border. The court said federal law lets the head of Homeland Security, Markwayne Mullin, set aside laws that protect nature so building can move faster.

The case was brought by the Center for Biological Diversity, a group that works to protect nature. Critics say the wall is not needed there, because the rough land and hot desert already make crossings rare.
why_it_matters: It matters because decisions about walls and wild land can change the places where animals live and where families visit nature.
